# Preface {.unnumbered}

This is the student-facing book for a four-week, ungraded elective on AI in
medicine for fourth-year medical students. Each chapter is one module: one to two
hours of reading, watching, and doing that stands alone, so a missed week costs
one chapter, not the course.

Every chapter follows the same shape:

1. **A scenario** — a clinical situation you will recognize, before any jargon
2. **Why this matters** — what changes in residency in three months
3. **The idea** — the concept, in prose, with figures and tables
4. **Watch or listen** — one video or podcast episode
5. **Do** — the activity, written so you can finish it alone; wherever it touches
   the literature, you choose your specialty
6. **Check** — a rubric you score yourself against
7. **The standing question** — *what does this change about how you'll practice?*
8. **Go deeper** — papers, talks, and videos, with unverified claims flagged

Three rules hold everywhere: **no patient information enters any tool, ever;
verify before it counts; you sign the note.**

Three ideas recur in every chapter. Proxies fail. Efficiency gains get eaten by
volume. The published number is the optimistic one. They are named the first time
they appear and called by name after that.

The design behind this book — competencies, constraints, schedule — lives in the
`curriculum/` directory of the repository.

**This book was built with AI.** The author directed and edited; an AI coding
assistant drafted most of the prose and looked up the references. How the book
was designed, how each chapter is reviewed, and what the AI did are in the
appendix [How this book was made](appendix/about.qmd) and the
[AI ledger](appendix/ai-ledger.qmd). The course asks you to disclose and verify;
this is the course doing the same.
